learning_extracted: 460l independently confirms the 460k wiring diagnosis from a clean foraging eval (no contract-harness injection): the closure-exclusive de-commit eval substrate (e52158d) does NOT arm the closure-coupled latch-hold in a real run -- ncl_hold_closure_armed_total=0 everywhere.

Maintenance cannot be the bottleneck if no maintained hold forms.

Narrow positive: the JOB-1 signed-RPE delta_t = R_t - V-hat_t (reused by the habenula) is LIVE and produces genuine negative-RPE variance in a real eval (n_neg_delta_ticks 834-1117, delta_t_min -0.42). The habenula's INPUT works; only the hold it would act on is absent.

The fix is substrate, not another test: make the closure-coupled commit arm a sustained hold independently of the F-driven e3._committed_trajectory (implement-substrate amend f_dominance_conversion_ceiling). Refuse a 460m re-queue (5th lineage iteration).
targets.recommended_epistemic_category_per_claim: Added 2026-07-21. This target's own .md (line 43) states: 'MECH-090 (BetaGate commit-entry conjunction), MECH-342 (maintenance-time release coupling): precondition/peripheral here (the latch and its release); NOT EXERCISED.' A claim the run did not exercise cannot supply evidence of a substrate ceiling FOR THAT CLAIM, so attributing the blanket substrate_ceiling category to MECH-342 false-fired the MOVE-3 re-derive brake against all future MECH-342 work -- the same inversion the brake's instrument-defect carve-out exists to prevent. The brake's own refusal_note scopes it to 'a V3-EXQ-460m same-claim re-queue' on the MECH-445/446 commitment-maintenance substrate (upstream f_dominance_conversion_ceiling), not to MECH-342. Corroborating: MECH-342's mechanism demonstrably FIRED correctly when it WAS exercised ecologically (629b seed 43: decommit_transitions=34, mech342_fires=1, beta occupancy 1.0->0.217 in the degraded window vs 1.0 in the OFF arm) -- not the signature of a claim at a substrate ceiling. SCOPE: only MECH-342 is re-attributed. MECH-090 is described by the same .md sentence and is likely the same misattribution, but its ceiling count is 7 (6 without this target) so it is not decision-relevant, and re-attributing it was left to governance rather than done in passing. Nothing else about this artifact's adjudication changes: recommended_evidence_direction_per_claim['MECH-342'] remains non_contributory, which is and always was correct.
